doc.title: Wilson "Chembo" Corniel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019

title: Novelty Latin hits, Macarena and Kenny G's Latin album
summary: He views such hits as business moves, praising Cyndi Lauper's Latin record and doubting Kenny G's.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Okay. Have there been tunes that have come along that you feel like pop hits — let me go back. Jazz musicians, when, like Kenny G came out, most of them were like sort of disgusted at what he was doing. I think it shouldn’t have been called jazz in the first place. But at any rate, like a tune like the Macarena in ’97, do those kinds of sort of novelty Latin hits bother you?

I see this is business you know. And he’s looking at it as the standpoint of that. Kenny G I think also, a couple of years ago recorded a Latin record, tried to do a Latin album so he could enter it into the Latin Grammys since it’s Kenny G — he thought maybe he would have a leg up on it or something, I don’t know because it’s Kenny G goes Latin. Cyndi Lauper did one but hers came out really good. Singing in English, Cyndi Lauper with real arrangements in clave, real musicians that know the stuff, and hip arrangements. But she sang in English, that was a killer. But Kenny G you know I see what you mean by that, because they’re trying to step in, and this is all for me, it’s more of a business kind of tactic, because musically it wasn’t going to go nowhere, because people who know music, and the general public, they hear Macarena, they’d rather hear the real one instead of a watered down one you know. So I guess he just tried to, it was an invention, or see where I can go with this, to open up another avenue where I can make money. Maybe I could hit the Latin market now, then I’ll do, whatever, you know, I’ll do “La Bamba” next or something. You know? Maybe I can get over that way. But tunes like the Macarena is more of like a Brazilian-based dance and stuff like that. So that’s not even hit the main street Latin market you know?
